newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan puts south state on alert after rebel gains.
newsitem.headline: Sudan puts south state on alert after rebel gains.

text.p: A Sudanese provincial governor said in remarks published on Sunday the government has put the southern Bahr el-Ghazal state on maximum alert after rebels captured several of its towns.
"All in the state are currently in a state of maximum alert," Ali Tamim Fartak, governor of the Western Bahr el-Ghazal province, was quoted by the government-owned Sudan al-Hadith daily as saying.

"The government, the national peace forces in the state and forces of Kerubino Kwanyin are (gathered) in one bunker for the defence of the nation," Fartak said. Kwanyin heads a southern armed faction which has made peace with the government.

The daily said the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), fighting the Islamist government for autonomy of the mainly Christian and animist south, had captured several towns in the Buheyrat and Warap areas. They include Rumbek, Tonj and Gogrial.
The head of the armed forces committee has asked that immediate aid be sent to Bahr el-Ghazal, the newspaper added.

Since January, the SPLA has joined forces with northern opposition groups to topple the Khartoum government. But reports of fighting have died down after initial claims by both sides of substantial gains.
